# fivenines_systemd_units (Data Source)

The per-unit health rows behind the instance's Services tab -- which units are failed, what systemd's own verdict was, and the journal tail captured at the moment each one broke. A metrics query can say HOW MANY units are failed; only this can name them.

The cgroup readings (`memory_current`, `cpu_usec`, `oom_kill_count`) are null when unavailable on the host, never 0 -- cgroup v1 has no OOM counter at all, and a 0 there would read as "nothing was OOM killed" when the truth is "we cannot see whether anything was". `reverse_deps` is null when the host's systemd is too old to report them, which is a different fact from `[]` ("nothing depends on this unit").

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Every systemd unit on a host
data "fivenines_systemd_units" "all" {
  instance_id = fivenines_instance.web.id
}

# Ask the API for the failed ones instead of filtering in HCL
data "fivenines_systemd_units" "failed" {
  instance_id  = fivenines_instance.web.id
  active_state = "failed"
  stale        = false # only rows the agent refreshed inside the sync window
}

# An empty list is not an all-clear on its own: the collector may be switched
# off (which deletes the rows) or the agent may be too old to report them.
output "units_are_healthy" {
  value = (
    data.fivenines_systemd_units.failed.collector.enabled &&
    data.fivenines_systemd_units.failed.collector.supported &&
    length(data.fivenines_systemd_units.failed.systemd_units) == 0
  )
}

output "failed_unit_names" {
  value = [for u in data.fivenines_systemd_units.failed.systemd_units : u.name]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID the rows belong to.

### Optional

- `active_state` (String) Filter by systemd's own ActiveState -- `failed` is the on-call filter. The column stores whatever systemd reported, verbatim; a state outside the documented list is still returned, it just cannot be selected by name. One of: `active`, `reloading`, `inactive`, `failed`, `activating`, `deactivating`, `maintenance`, `refreshing`.
- `q` (String) Case-insensitive substring match on the unit name.
- `stale` (Boolean) Freshness filter over the collector's 10-minute sync window. `false` returns only rows the agent refreshed inside it -- the set you may read as CURRENT state; `true` returns the rest. The two values partition the collection (a row that never synced counts as stale). Omit for both.
- `updated_since` (String) Return only rows whose `updated_at` is at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Inclusive, so a row updated in the same instant as the cursor comes back rather than falling through the gap. The ingester touches `updated_at` on every agent tick, so this is a freshness filter rather than a change feed, and there are no tombstones: a row the agent stops reporting is deleted.

### Read-Only

- `collector` (Attributes) Why the row list looks the way it does. Read this before treating an empty list as a clean bill of health: `[]` alone cannot distinguish "this host genuinely runs none" from "the collector is switched off" (which deletes the rows) or "this agent is too old to report them". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--collector))
- `systemd_units` (Attributes List) The rows the collector reported. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--systemd_units))

<a id="nestedatt--collector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `collector`

Read-Only:

- `blocked_reason` (String) The agent's own explanation, where it sent one. Null otherwise.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the operator has this collector switched on for the instance. Switching it off deletes the rows, so `false` fully explains an empty list.
- `last_reported_at` (String) The instance's last agent check-in -- not this collector's. It separates "this collector went quiet" (rows stale, instance reporting) from "the whole agent went quiet" (both). Per-row freshness is each row's `last_synced_at`.
- `name` (String) The collector these rows come from.
- `pending` (Boolean) Enabled, and the agent knows the feature, but the capability is not satisfied yet (missing binary, missing permission). The rows are legitimately absent and may appear on a later tick.
- `supported` (Boolean) Whether this agent can collect these rows -- its own capability verdict where it reports one, its version otherwise. `false` alongside `enabled` means the instance was asked for something it cannot deliver. Read it as "the agent has not said it cannot": the config-driven collectors (haproxy, rabbitmq, php_fpm, wireguard) have no version floor, so an agent predating one still reports `true` with an empty list.
- `unavailable_reason` (String) Why `supported` is false: `host_lacks_feature` (the agent probed and reported it cannot) or `agent_outdated` (the agent predates the release that collects these rows). Null when supported.


<a id="nestedatt--systemd_units"></a>
### Nested Schema for `systemd_units`

Read-Only:

- `active_enter_at` (String) When the unit last entered its active state. Null when systemd recorded no such transition.
- `active_state` (String) systemd's ActiveState, verbatim.
- `cpu_usec` (Number) Microseconds of CPU since unit start. **Null means unavailable, not 0.**
- `created_at` (String) When this row was first recorded. This is when the agent first happened to report it, not anything an operator would recognize.
- `drilldown_at` (String) When `journal_tail` / `reverse_deps` were captured.
- `failed` (Boolean) Whether systemd currently reports the unit as failed. The on-call signal.
- `host_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID this row belongs to.
- `id` (Number) Row identifier.
- `inactive_enter_at` (String) When the unit last entered its inactive state. Null when systemd recorded no such transition.
- `journal_tail` (List of String) Error-priority journal lines captured ONCE, at the moment the unit failed, and then kept. The ingester deliberately never clears these columns, so a unit that failed and later RECOVERED still carries the journal from that failure: a row can read `failed: false` / `active_state: active` and a non-empty `journal_tail` at the same time. Always read it against `drilldown_at` (when it was captured) and `active_state` (what the unit is doing now) -- it is last-failure evidence, not a statement about the current state. Empty only for a unit that has never failed.
- `last_synced_at` (String) Server arrival time of the tick that last refreshed this row (never the agent's clock).
- `load_state` (String) systemd's LoadState -- whether the unit file itself loaded (`loaded`, `not-found`, `masked`). Null when not reported.
- `memory_current` (Number) Bytes. **Null means unavailable on this host, not 0.**
- `n_restarts` (Number) systemd's NRestarts counter for the unit. **Null means unavailable, not 0.**
- `name` (String) The unit name, e.g. `nginx.service`. This is the row identity.
- `oom_kill_count` (Number) Kills since the unit started (the raw cgroup counter; the cgroup directory is recreated on restart). **Null means unavailable** -- cgroup v1 has no such counter -- and must not be read as "nothing was OOM killed".
- `result` (String) systemd's own verdict on the last run.
- `reverse_deps` (List of String) What depends on this unit. **Null means the host's systemd is too old to report them** (< 230) -- a different fact from `[]`, which means nothing depends on it.
- `since_at` (String) When the CURRENT state began -- `active_enter_at` for a running unit, `inactive_enter_at` otherwise. Null when systemd recorded no transition.
- `stale` (Boolean) True when the agent has not refreshed this row inside the 10-minute window. A stale row is a LAST KNOWN state, not a current one.
- `sub_state` (String) systemd's SubState, the unit-type-specific detail behind `active_state` (e.g. `running`, `dead`, `failed`). Null when not reported.
- `unit_file_state` (String) Whether the unit is enabled at boot (`enabled`, `disabled`, `static`, `masked`). Null when not reported.
- `updated_at` (String) When this row was last written. The ingester touches it on every agent tick, so it is a freshness stamp rather than a change feed.
